relationships.subject: vlPAG GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Together, our results collectively demonstrate that activation of vlPAGGABA+ neurons causes hypersensitivity to mechanical stimulation; however, their inhibition decreases the sensitivity to noxious heat only.

relationships.subject: DR GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Our data demonstrate that specific inhibition of DRGABA+ neurons causes mechanical hypersensitivity; however, the activation of these neurons has no obvious effect on anxiety-like behavior during naïve states.

relationships.subject: morphine
relationships.evidence_quote: we observed that the pronociceptive effect arising from DR<sup>GABA+</sup> neuronal inhibition was reversed by the systemic administration of morphine

key_findings: Chemogenetic co-activation of vlPAG-DR GABAergic neurons produced mechanical hyperalgesia and anxiety-like behavior, and their inhibition relieved CFA inflammatory pain.
vlPAG and DR GABAergic neurons have opposing roles: inhibition or ablation of DR GABAergic neurons caused mechanical hypersensitivity, while their activation relieved CFA-induced hyperalgesia.
